programme.title: The Tournament: A History of ACC Men's Basketball
programme.desc: When Indiana native Everett Case arrives in Raleigh to become the coach at North Carolina State, his vision spearheads not just the rise of college basketball at his school and in the region, but the start of a conference that will change the sport.

programme.desc: From Frank McGuire to Bones McKinney and Vic Bubas, new coaches emerge to challenge the early success of Everett Case. It all precedes a final poignant moment of triumph for Case at the only home the ACC Tournament has, until this point, ever known.

programme.title: The Tournament: A History of ACC Men's Basketball

programme.title: The Tournament: A History of ACC Men's Basketball

programme.desc: Weatherman Derek Brockway is on Gower, but he ignores the route along Worms Head taken by most walkers. Instead, he sets off along a less well-known stretch of coast, from Fall Bay to Oxwich, about eleven miles away.

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen Best Bites
programme.desc: Matt Tebbutt serves up some favourite recipes from years gone by. Pam Brunton prepares a rich, flavour-packed mushroom broth garnished with grilled squid, roasted onions and hen of the woods.

programme.title: A Cook Abroad
programme.desc: Scottish chef Tony Singh travels to India, the country of his ancestors, to trace his family roots and discover whether his mum's Punjabi cooking is the real deal. He begins his journey in Amritsar before braving the Grand Trunk Road to Delhi.

programme.title: ISU World Championship Figure Skating
programme.desc: Highlights from Boston, with ice dance pair Lilah Fear and Lewis Gibson vying to win Britain's first World Championship medal since Jayne Torvill and Christopher Dean in 1984. Fear and Gibson already have three European Championship medals, including bronze at 2025's event in Estonia, but have ended fourth at each of the past two World Championships. Home favourites Madison Chock and Evan Bates will be looking to defend their ice dance title.

programme.title: This Farming Life
programme.desc: It's shearing time for the Imries, but their minds are on their next big event: a family music festival. Once the farm work is done, it's full steam ahead with preparations. They are relying on last-minute ticket sales to make a profit.

programme.title: The Wonder of Animals
programme.desc: Chris Packham examines the penguin's anatomy, to reveal how its wings and body shape have allowed it to conquer an extraordinary range of habitats, from forests, to tropical waters, cities and even the toughest place on the planet, Antarctica.

programme.title: The Great Gatsby
programme.desc: At the centre of the story is Jay Gatsby, whose lust for money and power conceals a deeper passion, his love for Daisy, the woman he met in his early youth but lost to the bullying but wealthy Tom Buchanan. His millions made, Gatsby moves into a mansion close to Daisy, where he holds lavish parties, hoping to win her back.

programme.title: New York: America's Busiest City
programme.desc: Ade heads to Harlem and meets residents who are benefiting and suffering at the hands of gentrification. The price of a townhouse here has gone from $50,000 to over $4 million in 30 years. Ant is at Hudson Yards on the west side of Manhattan where an entirely new district is being built on top of a functioning rail depot. It's an innovative building solution to the island's lack of land.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Paul Martin presents from Norwich cathedral in Norfolk, once home to Benedictine monks, and he also visits the circus. Experts Thomas Plant and Kate Bateman pick out some gems to take to auction, among them a religious relic from France and a Martin brothers vase.

programme.title: This Farming Life
programme.desc: On Papay, Paul and Mel juggle farm work with wedding prep, while Sally's ewes in Caithness have been struck by a mystery illness. Jo and Andy turn lambs into much-needed cash.

programme.title: Expedition with Steve Backshall
programme.desc: Steve Backshall leads a team of elite explorers, including world leading underwater cave explorer Robbie Schmittner, former Royal Marine Aldo Kane and diving camera operator, Katy Fraser, into the wilds of the Yucatan Peninsula in Mexico. Under the vast jungle here is the largest unexplored network of caves in the world, comprising thousands of kilometres of passageways.

programme.title: Amazing Hotels: Life Beyond the Lobby
programme.desc: Monica Galetti and Rob Rinder travel to Kasbah Tamadot in the Atlas Mountains of Morocco. With Sir Richard Branson as their boss, they discover how genuine Berber hospitality and spectacular views of the landscape make it unique.

programme.title: Tribe with Bruce Parry
programme.desc: Deep in the Amazon, Bruce Parry undergoes a brutal training regime to prepare his mind and body to take ayahuasca and understand how the Waimaha connect with the forest around them.

programme.title: Allelujah
